item.text:
### (a) Three posts

1. If superintelligent AI is built within the next 20 years, most countries will lose the ability to defend themselves. We must confront that prospect now—not after the power to protect our societies has slipped away.

2. We cannot build national security on the assumption that today’s defences will hold tomorrow. If superintelligent AI is built within the next 20 years, most countries will lose the ability to defend themselves. We need prevention, not complacency.

3. We reject a future in which sovereignty exists on paper but countries cannot protect their people. If superintelligent AI is built within the next 20 years, most countries will lose the ability to defend themselves. We must act before that future arrives.

### (b) Newsletter opening

If superintelligent AI is built within the next 20 years, most countries will lose the ability to defend themselves. We see this as a fundamental threat to sovereignty, public safety and our collective freedom to determine our future. We cannot accept a race in which the pursuit of technological dominance overrides everyone else’s security. Nor can we treat existing military strength as a permanent guarantee of protection. We need binding international limits, meaningful oversight and the political courage to put safety before speed. We must insist that our governments confront this threat now, while we still have the power to choose a different path.
